ig_caption:
Myth: to pay estimated tax right, you have to guess this year's income exactly.
Fact: the IRS gives you a safe number you already know: last year's tax.

✔️ Pay at least 100% of the tax on your 2025 return, spread over the four payments, and most people avoid the underpayment penalty.
✔️ If your 2025 AGI was over $150,000 ($75,000 married filing separately), use 110%.
✔️ Or pay 90% of your 2026 tax, whichever is smaller. Owe under $1,000 after withholding? No penalty.

Example: your 2025 tax was $8,000. Paying $2,000 a quarter covers you, even if 2026 was a bigger year. You settle the rest in April.

The last 2026 payment is due January 15, 2027. State rules vary (NJ and NY have their own).

li_caption:
Many self-employed owners skip estimated tax payments because they can't predict this year's income. The IRS rules give a simpler starting point.

Most people avoid the underpayment penalty if any one of these is true:

1. They owe less than $1,000 after withholding and credits.
2. They paid at least 90% of the tax for the current year.
3. They paid at least 100% of the tax shown on last year's return, spread over the four payment dates. If last year's AGI was over $150,000 ($75,000 married filing separately), the figure is 110%.

Option 3 uses a number you already know. Example: 2025 tax of $8,000 means $2,000 a quarter covers the penalty test, even if 2026 profit doubled. The balance is due in April.

The last 2026 payment is due January 15, 2027. Filing the 2026 return by January 31 and paying in full also works. State rules differ; New Jersey and New York set their own.

We set up 2027 estimates for business owners so each payment is planned, not guessed.

sources.fact: Individuals generally must pay estimated tax if they expect to owe $1,000 or more; most avoid the penalty if they owe less than $1,000 after withholding and credits, or paid at least 90% of the current-year tax or 100% of the prior-year tax, whichever is smaller (IRS Estimated taxes page, read 2026-11-18)

Higher income taxpayers: if 2025 AGI was more than $150,000 ($75,000 if 2026 status is married filing separately), substitute 110% for 100%; fourth 2026 payment due January 15, 2027; if the 2026 return is filed by January 31, 2027 and the rest of the tax is paid, the January 15 payment is not needed (Pub 505 (2026), read 2026-11-18)
NJ-1040-ES and NY IT-2105 fourth 2026 payments also due Jan 15, 2027 (repo data/tax-calendar-2027.json, checked 2026-10-20)
$8,000 / $2,000 a quarter example is an illustration (100% of prior-year tax / 4), not a client or statistic
